_comment: Scenario templates: opinionated PRESETS that arrange the sandbox into a recognizable mission, filtered by map/era/needs_carrier. Each carries a recipe preset (applied by the frontend to pre-fill the wizard, editable) and a 'brief' tasking block (appended to the mission briefing by the builder - suggested tasking only, NO forced waypoints). These are distinct from the crew-ops templates (backseat_*/rio_fleet_defense) which are handled by dedicated builder branches.

carrier_qual.label: Carrier Qualification (CQ) — Case I/III recovery practice at the boat
brief: === TASKING (suggested) — CARRIER QUALIFICATION ===
The boat is steaming into the wind with the pattern open. Fly the case:
- CASE I (day/VMC): overhead break, downwind, groove. Fuel state to Marshal.
- CASE III (night/IMC): Marshal stack, push on time, CATCC/ACLS approach.
Recovery tanker is overhead for your bolters and low-state passes. No enemy
tasking - this is currency and traps. Grade yourself: bolter, 1-wire to OK-3.

library.premise: Traps at the boat — pattern work until your boarding rate is where you want it. Calm deck, empty jet.

acls_practice.label: ACLS Practice — Mode I/IA coupled approaches (SuperCarrier)
brief: === TASKING (suggested) — ACLS PRACTICE ===
SuperCarrier boat, Link4 + ACLS radiating (see the Boat Card for channels).
Work the coupled approach:
- Fly to Marshal, set Link4 (F/A-18: DL20; F-14 RIO enters the freq), ICLS on.
- Commence, needles/ACLS: Mode II (needles, you fly) then Mode I (coupled,
hands-off to touchdown) once you trust the datalink.
Tanker overhead for the go-arounds. Night/weather is set to make it count.
Note: ACLS needs an ACLS-capable hull (SuperCarrier / Stennis) - keep the
carrier on a supercarrier and don't swap to the Forrestal for this one.

library.premise: Mode I/IA coupled approach — fly the needles down to a hands-off night trap in the weather.

cap_alert5.label: CAP / Alert-5 — hold the line, intercept inbound raiders
brief: === TASKING (suggested) — COMBAT AIR PATROL ===
You own a CAP station on the threat axis. AWACS has the picture; check in and
work the intercepts. Enemy CAP is up and probing - expect commit calls.
Tanker on station to keep you on the wall. ROE: your call - this is a training
furball, not a scored engagement. Hold the line, protect the rear, RTB with gas.

library.premise: Hold the line. Sit Alert-5 and scramble to intercept inbound raiders before they reach the fleet.

sead_range.label: SEAD / Wild Weasel Range — work a defended target complex
brief: === TASKING (suggested) — SEAD / WILD WEASEL ===
A defended target area is up ahead - SAM belt around the enemy fields (see the
F10 threat rings and the kneeboard). Roll back the air defenses:
- First on the RWR, sort the emitters, respect the rings.
- HARM/Shrike the acquisition and TR radars; re-attack the shooters.
AWACS has the picture, tanker's behind you. No fixed waypoints - build your own
ingress around the threats. Success = you can fly the target area without a launch.

library.premise: Wild Weasel work over a defended target — bait the SAMs, kill the radars, open the door for the strikers.

berlin_corridor_transit.label: Berlin Corridor Transit — fly the Cold War air corridors to Berlin
brief: === TASKING (suggested) — BERLIN CORRIDOR TRANSIT ===
Three 20-mile-wide corridors run across GDR airspace to West Berlin, ceiling
10,000 ft, all converging on the Berlin Control Zone (see the F10 map — violet
swaths — and the airspace note below). This is an airspace-discipline sortie:
- Pick a corridor (North/Hamburg, Center/Hannover, South/Frankfurt) and hold
inside its lateral limits, below the ceiling, all the way to the Control Zone.
- Straying out over GDR territory is what got you intercepted historically —
the win here is a clean transit, not a fight.
No enemy tasking, no fixed waypoints. Fly the lanes, respect the ceiling, RTB.

library.premise: Thread the real Cold-War air corridors into Berlin — stay in the lane, the whole world is watching.

af_tic_cas.label: Troops in Contact — Ridge-Line CAS (Kandahar A-10)

library.premise: A JTAC has troops pinned on a ridge in the green zone. Check in, get eyes on, and put warheads on foreheads — danger close.

brief: == TASKING: TROOPS IN CONTACT ==
Friendly patrol in contact in the target area (see F10 + kneeboard).
Check in with AWACS, work the target package as your JTAC talk-on.
Threats are SHORAD/MANPADS class - keep smart altitudes between attacks.

af_bastion_scramble.label: Bastion Scramble — Harrier Alert (VMA-211)

library.premise: Alert Harrier at Camp Bastion. The QRF needs air NOW — runway alert, first pass counts.

brief: == TASKING: ALERT LAUNCH ==
Immediate launch from Bastion alert. Strike package in the target area.
Fuel is tight - Texaco is airborne if you need it.

af_convoy_overwatch.label: Helmand Convoy Overwatch (F-16 night)

library.premise: A logistics convoy is threading the Helmand river road after dark. Own the overhead, find the ambush before it happens.

brief: == TASKING: CONVOY OVERWATCH ==
Convoy route and target package marked on the F10 map.
Work the targeting pod down the route ahead of the convoy;
strike only positively identified threats - ROE is tight tonight.

af_hindu_kush_qra.label: Hindu Kush QRA — Northern Intercept

library.premise: Fast movers pushing south over the Hindu Kush. Scramble from Kandahar, climb hard, and meet them in the high passes.

brief: == TASKING: QUICK REACTION ALERT ==
Overlord holds the picture - expect bandits from the northern fields.
The terrain is the second enemy: MSA in the passes is unforgiving.
Bagram's SAM umbrella is active - respect the rings on the F10 map.
